ComBat-refQL adjusts RNA-seq counts toward one observed reference batch. The
method combines QL-moderated batch-effect estimation, hierarchical
reference-centred NB dispersion, counterfactual prediction, and deterministic
count transport. Biological groups and supplied covariates remain in the mean
model throughout.

## Mean model and estimand

After TMMwsp normalization, ComBat-refQL fits

$$
\log\mu_{gj}=\log L_j+X_j\beta_g+\gamma_{g,b(j)},
$$

where $L_j$ is the effective library size, $X_j$ contains biological variables,
and $\gamma_{g,b(j)}$ is the gene-specific batch coefficient. For reference
batch $r$, the source-batch estimand is

$$\delta_{gb}=\gamma_{gb}-\gamma_{gr}.$$

The design must be full rank. Batch contrasts require biological overlap that
identifies batch separately from biology.

## QL uncertainty and empirical-Bayes moderation

The final edgeR v4 fit supplies an exact source-versus-reference contrast and
its moderated QL-scaled variance:

$$
\widehat\delta_{gb}\mid\delta_{gb}\approx
N(\delta_{gb},s^2_{gb,\mathrm{QL}}).
$$

For every non-reference batch, ComBat-refQL fits one heteroscedastic normal
prior,

$$\delta_{gb}\sim N(m_b,\tau_b^2),$$

by profile marginal maximum likelihood. The posterior mean is

$$
\widetilde\delta_{gb}=
\frac{\tau_b^2}{\tau_b^2+s^2_{gb,\mathrm{QL}}}\widehat\delta_{gb}+
\frac{s^2_{gb,\mathrm{QL}}}{\tau_b^2+s^2_{gb,\mathrm{QL}}}m_b.
$$

Precise contrasts stay near their fitted values; uncertain contrasts move
toward the batch prior mean. At $\tau_b^2=0$, supported contrasts pool to
$m_b$. Invalid uncertainty and insufficient supported genes receive explicit
diagnostic status.

QL quasi-dispersion quantifies uncertainty in the fitted mean coefficients. It
never enters a negative-binomial probability calculation.

## Hierarchical batch-specific NB dispersion

ComBat-refQL models the NB dispersion as

$$
\log\phi_{gb}=f(A_g)+u_g+d_b,\qquad d_r=0,
$$

or equivalently

$$\phi_{gb}=\phi_{gr}\exp(d_b).$$

`edgeR::estimateDisp()` supplies the moderated gene baseline. A weighted NB
likelihood estimates one batch-wide multiplier for each batch; 0.4.0 contains
no gene-by-batch dispersion interaction. The mean model is then refitted using
the resulting gene-by-sample NB dispersion matrix.

## Effective residual information

The initial design diagnostic is

$$H^{(0)}=X(X^TX)^{-1}X^T,$$

and its batch contribution is

$$\nu_b^{(0)}=\sum_{j:b(j)=b}(1-h^{(0)}_{jj}).$$

After preliminary fitting, working weights define

$$H_g=W_g^{1/2}X(X^TW_gX)^{-1}X^TW_g^{1/2},$$

$$\nu_{gb}=\sum_{j:b(j)=b}(1-h_{gjj}).$$

The dispersion precision contribution is

$$p_{gb}=\{\psi_1(\nu_{gb}/2)\}^{-1}.$$

This contribution increases continuously with residual information and is zero
when the stratum is saturated. A source batch with no dispersion information
receives the identified neutral shift $d_b=0$ and `not_estimable` status. The
reference batch must contain positive dispersion information; otherwise the
fit raises a typed statistical error.

## Counterfactual mean and deterministic transport

For a source observation, the reference-counterfactual mean is

$$\mu^{(r)}_{gj}=\mu_{gj}\exp(-\widetilde\delta_{gb}).$$

Given observed count $y$, ComBat-refQL calculates

$$
q=F_b(y-1;\mu_{gj},\phi_{gb})+
\tfrac12P_b(Y=y;\mu_{gj},\phi_{gb}),
$$

then maps to

$$y^*=F_r^{-1}(q;\mu^{(r)}_{gj},\phi_{gr}).$$

For $y=0$, this gives $q=\tfrac12P_b(Y=0)$. Tail probabilities are clipped to
finite machine-safe bounds. Transport is deterministic and chunk size changes
allocation only. A numerical failure rolls the complete gene row back to its
original counts.

## Reference selection and preservation

An explicit reference provides the clearest target. With `reference = NULL`,
ComBat-refQL builds a locally estimable biological design in each batch, fits
an edgeR candidate model, and selects the smallest valid NB score. Diagnostics
retain every score, the runner-up, the margin, and local-design details.

Reference samples bypass transport. The implementation verifies exact equality
between input and output reference counts before constructing the result.

## Interpreting adjusted counts

Adjusted counts represent a model-based reference-batch counterfactual. They
support batch-aligned visualization, exploratory analysis, and workflows that
require count-scale data. Differential-expression inference uses the original
counts with batch and biological variables represented in the statistical
design.
